claim: For every integer \(n\ge 6\), let \(\operatorname{Cr}_n=K_{n,n}-M_n\) be the crown graph with deleted matching \(M_n=\{a_i b_i:1\le i\le n\}\). Its majority C-chromatic number is exactly \(\overline{\chi}_{\geqslant}(\operatorname{Cr}_n)=2\). Moreover, all optimal two-colorings can be classified from the two index sets \(S=\{i:a_i\text{ has color }1\}\) and \(T=\{i:b_i\text{ has color }1\}\). If \(n=2r\), then necessarily \(|S|=|T|=r\) and \(T=[n]\setminus S\), so there are \(\binom{n}{n/2}\) optimal colorings with the labeled palette \(\{1,2\}\). If \(n=2r+1\), then \((|S|,|T|,|S\cap T|)\) is exactly one of \((r,r,0)\), \((r,r+1,0)\), \((r+1,r,0)\), or \((r+1,r+1,1)\); hence the number of labeled optimal colorings is \((n+3)\binom{n}{(n-1)/2}\).
integrity: The universal upper bound, constructions, optimizer classification, and counting formulas are proved analytically. The bundled program independently tests the original neighborhood condition on finite instances and is used only as a stress test. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: The exact theorem is restricted to crown graphs with n at least 6 and the one-half open-neighborhood majority C threshold. It does not treat arbitrary matching deletions or classify nonoptimal colorings. An older satisfactory-partition source was accessible only at abstract level, leaving a stated residual literature risk.
title: Majority C-colorings of crown graphs
